references.text: Pharaoh appoints Joseph to be over all Egypt, which underscores the full authority he was given.
Joseph is the one everyone must turn to in order to buy grain, reflecting the authority and control he was granted over all Egypt.
Joseph explains that it was God who sent him to Egypt and set him as master over Pharaoh's entire household, mirroring his exalted position.
The psalm describes how Joseph was made ruler over Pharaoh's house and lord over everything he owned, a poetic rendering of his authority.
Stephen refers to how God gave Joseph grace and wisdom before Pharaoh, who set him as leader over Egypt and his entire household.
41:55 is the practical fulfillment of the authority granted in 41:44.
Theological contrast: God's hand saves Egypt through Joseph (41:44) but punishes Egypt to free Israel (Exod 7:4).
45:9 confirms and looks back to the authority given in 41:44 as a result of God's plan.
Contrast in Pharaoh's responsiveness: He listens to God's wisdom for salvation (41:44) but not to the prophet's message of liberation (Exod 11:9).
Theological contrast: Pharaoh's heart is soft enough to heed God for salvation (41:44) but hardened to resist liberation (Exod 4:21).
